Project Intake Form (Existing System)

# Project Intake Form (Existing System)

## Metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | bevy_markup (crate `bevy_markup`, called `p23` until 2026-10-05) |
| Repository | `github.com/nchashch/bevy_markup` (branch `main`; 313 commits since 2026-10-04); published on crates.io, 0.7.0 (2026-10-15) |
| Intake type | Existing system (brownfield), generated by `intake-from-codebase` |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0001–0034, the bug ledger (bug_0001–0180), the ADR 0034 trial report, `UPSTREAM.md`, reviews 0001–0006, `CHANGELOG.md`, CI history |
| Source state | commit `cf0da55` (2026-10-28; ADR 0034 accepted, parcel_selectors matching, new testbench scenarios) |
| Date | 2026-10-28 |
| Owner | Nikita Chashchinskii |

This page summarises; `AGENTS.md` (current state) and the ADRs (why) are authoritative.

## System Overview

A Bevy 0.20 library that turns HTML templates (Tera, or Markdown), CSS and Fluent localization into native Bevy UI entities, with 9-slice frames as CSS `border-image`. Apps spawn an `HtmlUi` with a template and a `TemplateContext`; the library renders, localizes and builds the entity tree, then updates it in place when the context, stylesheet, locale or interaction state changes. Declarative interaction (`data-on-*` signals, `:hover`/`:focus` restyles), focus and directional navigation, tooltips and anchored overlays, forms and text input are built in. It is the UI layer of the studio's games (prototype_19) and apps (vtuber).

## Problem and Outcomes

- Author game UI the way the web does (templates, stylesheets, translation files) instead of hand-built Bevy node trees.
- Keep the library to that mapping (ADR 0002): minimal Bevy features, app decisions (input bindings, fonts, panels) stay in apps.
- Verify the mapping against reference implementations (Chromium, `@fluent/dom`) and attack it with generated input (ADR 0004).

## Current Scope and Features

| Feature | State | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tera templates, Markdown templates (pulldown-cmark, converted at load) | built | ADR 0001, 0014, 0020 |
| CSS selectors matched by lightningcss's engine (parcel_selectors) within an allowlist: combinators (`+`/`~` next to the subject), `:is()`/`:where()`/`:not()` with lists, structural incl. `:nth-last-*`/`:only-*`, interaction pseudo-classes, `data-*` attributes with every operator | built (engine since 2026-10-28) | ADR 0007, 0028, 0030, 0034 |
| Sibling combinators away from the subject, non-`data-*` attributes, `:has()`, `:root` | not supported (restyle invalidation; the element model; engine gaps) | ADR 0034 |
| Layout: flex, grid (named lines and areas), positioning, `calc()`; tables and lists on the flex model | built | ADR 0007, 0027, 0028 |
| Text: fonts with fallback lists, `text-align`, `line-height`, `white-space`, `text-transform`, decorations | built | ADR 0015, 0027, 0028 |
| 9-slice frames (`border-image`), background images | built | ADR 0003, 0028 |
| Fluent localization (`data-l10n-*`, plurals, overlays); locale swap at runtime | built | ADR 0013 |
| In-place updates: identical renders skipped, keyed reconciliation, unchanged subtrees reused, scoped restyles, windowed build for long documents | built | ADR 0005, 0009, 0017, 0021, 0029, 0031–0033 |
| Signals (`data-on-*`), routing by name, forms with submit payload | built | ADR 0006, 0011 |
| Focus and directional navigation, modals; tooltips and anchors to elements and world points | built | ADR 0008, 0010 |
| Custom elements (`is=` + app system), text input (`text-input` feature) | built | ADR 0012, 0016, 0022, 0023 |
| SVG, `@media`, shadows, gradients as images, `@keyframes` | planned (roadmap tier 4) | ADR 0028 |
| `position: sticky`, `<textarea>`, built-in checkbox/radio | deferred (Bevy lacks the capability) | ADR 0028 |

## Architecture (Current State)

A `PostUpdate` pipeline in three chained sets (`HtmlUiSystems::{Render, Localize, Build}`) before Bevy's `UiSystems::Prepare`: render the Tera template, parse it (`astral-tl`), localize with Fluent, cascade the CSS (`lightningcss`; selectors matched by parcel_selectors over the walk's ancestor chain and sibling lists, `src/cascade/selector.rs`, ADR 0034), and reconcile a `NodeSpec` tree with the existing entities. When to update is decided by a pure state machine (`rebuild` module, ADR 0005). Details: @AGENTS.md ("Public API", "Layout", "Pipeline").

## Scale and Performance (Current)

Measured with criterion (600 elements): changing content 1.17 ms with subtree reuse (2.09 ms without), markdown 6.27 ms (ADR 0021). Benchmarks (criterion, divan) run nightly; hotpath profiling has a regression policy (`hotpath/policy.toml`). Long scrolling documents build only the visible band (ADR 0031–0033).

## Security and Compliance (Current)

- Template, CSS, Fluent and Markdown input are treated as untrusted: anything reachable from user data that panics is a high-severity bug; fuzzed by cargo-fuzz (`css`, `html`, `ftl`), honggfuzz, fuzzcheck, test-fuzz and arbtest.
- Two upstream `fluent-syntax` defects (a panic, a stack overflow) are fixed in a fork applied with `[patch.crates-io]`; apps must add the same patch (README). Upstream PRs pending (`UPSTREAM.md` U1, U2).
- The `dev-tools` QA surface (localhost BRP + MCP) is never enabled in a shipped build.
- MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## Team and Operations (Current)

One developer with AI coding agents (Claude Code, omp with other models); ADRs, bug reports for every defect, whole-crate review sessions (six so far), `CHANGELOG.md` per user-visible change. CI on every push (`ci.yml`), nightly (golden images, browser oracle, fuzzing, coverage, benchmarks), mutation testing (`mutants.yml`), shared build caches (`cache.yml`). Commits go straight to `main`.

## Dependencies and Infrastructure

| Dependency | Use |
|---|---|
| Bevy 0.20 (`default-features = false`, `ui_api` and a few more) | engine, UI, picking |
| tera, astral-tl, lightningcss, fluent, pulldown-cmark | templates, HTML parsing, CSS, localization, Markdown |
| parcel_selectors `=0.28.3` (lightningcss's selector engine, pinned to its version) | selector matching (ADR 0034) |
| fluent-syntax fork (`[patch.crates-io]`) | fixes for U1, U2 |
| bevy_mcp_harness (`dev-tools`) | agent QA of the examples |
| GitHub Actions (Ubuntu runner, lavapipe as the canonical renderer) | CI, nightly, mutants |
| Consumers: prototype_19 (0.4.0), vtuber (0.7.0) | studio users |

## Known Issues and Technical Debt

- The nightly workflow has failed every night since 2026-10-14 (2026-10-28: browser oracle drift, a css fuzz timeout, a stack overflow in the coverage job's corpus replay); not triaged.
- `flex-shrink` defaults to 0, not CSS's 1: copied browser CSS misbehaves silently (bug_0028; open design question).
- `CHANGELOG.md` has a large `[Unreleased]` section since 0.7.0; prototype_19 is still on 0.4.0.
- Known limits per area (layout, selectors, inline boxes, text, fonts): @AGENTS.md "Limits and next steps".

## Why This Intake Now?

Third member of the studio's AIWG workspace (root `../aiwg`): give the repository a requirements baseline, risk register and test strategy derived from its records.

## Attachments

- @.aiwg/intake/solution-profile.md
- @.aiwg/intake/option-matrix.md
- @.aiwg/requirements/use-cases.md
- @.aiwg/requirements/supplementary-spec.md
- @.aiwg/risks/risk-list.md
- @.aiwg/testing/test-strategy.md
- @.aiwg/testing/defect-register.md

## Next Steps

From `AGENTS.md` and ADR 0028: the tier-4 authoring gaps (SVG, `@media`, shadows, gradients, `@keyframes`), more test vectors with each; a deliberate decision on `flex-shrink`.

- @AGENTS.md
- @CHANGELOG.md

- @docs/agents/adr/0001-html-tera-fluent-css-onto-bevy-ui.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0002-library-shape-and-public-api.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0004-verification-strategy.md

Solution Profile (Current System)

# Solution Profile (Current System)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0004, 0018, 0019, 0021, 0028, bug ledger, `UPSTREAM.md`, CI history |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

## Current Profile

**Published library, early versions (0.x), used by the studio's own projects.** Verification is far above the norm for its size: reference oracles (Chromium styles and layout, `@fluent/dom`), golden images, property, stateful and model-based tests, five fuzzing drivers, mutation testing, coverage per testing layer, benchmarks. The weak spot is operations: the nightly workflow that runs the oracles, fuzzers and coverage has been red for two weeks without triage.

| Dimension | Level | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Security | Strong for scope | untrusted-input stance, fuzzing, two upstream panics patched (U1, U2) |
| Reliability | High | 176 of 178 filed bugs fixed with regression tests; pure update state machine; schedule-order shuffling in every test run |
| Testing & quality | Very high | oracles, golden images, property/model tests, fuzzing, mutants, coverage (88–98 % by layer) |
| Process rigor | High | 34 ADRs (0034 accepted after a measured trial), bug reports, six review sessions, changelog convention, CI on every push |
| Operations | Medium | nightly red since 2026-10-14; releases lag `main` (large `[Unreleased]`) |

## Recommended Profile Adjustments

- Triage the nightly failures and get it green again; treat a red nightly as a reason to file bugs, not noise (R-001).
- Release the `[Unreleased]` work and move prototype_19 off 0.4.0 (R-004).

## Improvement Roadmap

1. ADR 0028 tier 4: SVG, `@media`, shadows, gradients, `@keyframes`.
2. Decide `flex-shrink` deliberately (re-derive the vectors against browser defaults).
3. Get the fluent-syntax fixes merged upstream so apps no longer need the patch.

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0004-verification-strategy.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0021-per-element-dirty-tracking.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0028-modern-authoring-gaps-roadmap.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/INDEX.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/UPSTREAM.md

Test Strategy

# Test Strategy

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `test/test-strategy-template.md` (condensed) |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Testing", "Verification"), `docs/agents/skills/testing.md`, ADRs 0004, 0018, 0019 |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

## Context and Objectives

The library's promise is that HTML/CSS/Fluent behave as an author expects and that no input breaks it. ADR 0004 sets the method: verify against reference implementations (Chromium, `@fluent/dom`), then attack with every kind of generated input. Agents change the code often, so the suite is the safety net. How-to: @docs/agents/skills/testing.md.

## Test Levels and Scope

| Level | What | Where | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | cascade, templates and entities, l10n, fonts, 9-slice, rebuild state machine | `src/*` `#[cfg(test)]` | every push |
| Test vectors | inputs → text dump of the built world (25 vector directories plus inline vectors; `selectors_level4` since ADR 0034) | `tests/html_ui.rs`, `tests/vectors/` | every push |
| Oracles | computed styles and layout vs Chromium; localized output vs `@fluent/dom` | `browser_oracle`, `layout_oracle`, `fluent_oracle` | every push; nightly re-checks Chrome |
| Interaction | signals over the real picking stack; property test against a reference model | `tests/signals.rs`, `tests/signal_properties.rs` | every push |
| Property and model-based | layout invariants, selector model (Level 4 grammar since ADR 0034), stateful op sequences, windowing model, quickcheck, arbtest | `tests/layout_properties.rs`, `selector_model.rs`, `stateful.rs`, `windowing_model.rs`, `quickcheck.rs`, `arbtest.rs` | every push |
| Lints | examples' content (locales, templates, CSS); library source (no prints, no file writes) | `tests/content_lint.rs`, `tests/source_lint.rs` | every push |
| Golden images | rendered scenes vs references on lavapipe | `tests/golden.rs`, `scripts/golden.sh` | nightly (ignored locally without the flag) |
| Fuzzing | cargo-fuzz `css`/`html`/`ftl` (15 min each, corpora persisted), honggfuzz, fuzzcheck, test-fuzz; corpus replay | `fuzz/`, `honggfuzz/`, `fuzzcheck/`, `test-fuzz/`, `tests/fuzz_corpus.rs` | nightly |
| Mutation | cargo-mutants, sharded | `mutants.yml` | scheduled |
| Coverage | line coverage per testing layer | `scripts/coverage.py` | nightly |
| Performance | criterion and divan suites (incl. the selector-heavy `selectors` workload); hotpath policy | `benches/`, `hotpath/policy.toml` | nightly |
| Visual / agent | screenshots and playtests of the examples | `--features dev-tools`, bevy_mcp_harness | by hand |

**In scope:** the library and its examples. **Out of scope:** Bevy itself, the apps using the library (they test their own UI), upstream crates (tracked in `UPSTREAM.md`).

## Automation Strategy

`ci.yml` on every push and PR: warning-free checks and docs, `cargo test` (all of the push-time levels above), the Fluent oracle regeneration check. `nightly.yml`: golden images, browser oracle vs current Chrome, fuzzing, coverage, benchmarks — failures are reports to triage, not merge blockers. `cache.yml` builds shared caches once. Schedule order is shuffled in every test run.

Status on 2026-10-28: CI green on the last push; the nightly red every night since 2026-10-14 (risk R-001).

## Defect Management

Every defect gets `docs/agents/bugs/bug_NNNN.md` with discovery, minimal reproduction, root cause, fix commit and regression test; ledger in `INDEX.md`; upstream defects in `UPSTREAM.md`; whole-crate review sessions in `docs/agents/reviews/`. Index: @.aiwg/testing/defect-register.md.

## Requirements and Risk Coverage

Each requirement's "Verified by" column in @.aiwg/requirements/supplementary-spec.md names its check. No automated check: NFR-CONF-005, NFR-SUP-003, NFR-SUP-006, NFR-SEC-004 (conventions). Coverage was last measured at 88.1 % merged over ~3112 lines (2026-10-05); mutation results and coverage are read together (`AGENTS.md`).

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/skills/testing.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0004-verification-strategy.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0018-benchmarks-with-criterion.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0019-benchmarks-with-divan.md
- @docs/agents/performance/adr-0034-trial.md

# Defect Register

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Derived from | `docs/agents/bugs/INDEX.md`, `UPSTREAM.md`, `docs/agents/reviews/`, CI history |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

An index; the bug reports are authoritative. 180 reports, bug_0001–0180 (2026-10-04 to 2026-10-28).

## By Status and Severity

| Status | Count |
|---|---|
| Fixed, with regression test | 178 |
| Won't fix (known limit) | 1 — bug_0170, a one-frame row shift in the windowed build (low) |
| Withdrawn (not a bug) | 1 — bug_0026 |

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| High (reachable from user data, panics included) | 48 |
| Medium | 77 (+1 low–medium) |
| Low | 53 |

No open bugs.

## How They Were Found

Property testing, stateful testing and fuzzing (bug_0001–0005), the Fluent and layout oracles (0006–0013), mutation-testing triage, corpus coverage replays, example smoke runs, prototype_19 integration (0021), user reports (0023, 0028–0030), and whole-crate review sessions: review_0001–0006 found most of bug_0031 onward, each finding filed when its fix landed. Per-session metadata in `INDEX.md`.

## Upstream Defects (`UPSTREAM.md`)

U1–U15: lightningcss exponential parsing and unbounded recursion (U14, U15; worked around by the nesting pre-scan), fluent-syntax panic and stack overflow (forked, PR pending), pulldown-cmark panic (U13, fixed by updating), honggfuzz-rs, fuzzcheck (three, vendored patches), cargo-mutants, cargo-fuzz, Bevy picking (two), lightningcss, tl (switched to `astral-tl`).

## Nightly Failures (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-28, fixed on `main`)

| Job | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Fuzz css (timeouts) | lightningcss parses nested `light-dark(` / `calc(var(…))` in exponential time, inside the old 32-block bound | bug_0179: paren bound 8 |
| Coverage (stack overflow in `replay_css_corpus`) | the css harness skipped the loader's nesting pre-scan; lightningcss recursion is unbounded | bug_0179: the harness applies the pre-scan |
| Browser oracle | `tests/vectors/text_props` had no `browser.json`; the oracle script recorded text without `text-transform` | the script reads rendered text; reference committed |

The ADR 0034 trial's differential run found one more old-matcher defect, fixed by the engine without a bug report: `:nth-child(0)` matched the root (CHANGELOG "Fixed"; test `nth_child_zero_matches_no_element`).

The timeouts had masked bug_0180 (a panic in `Compound::parse`), found by a local fuzz run after the fix.

# AIWG.md
<!-- aiwg-managed -->
<!-- CLAUDE.md companion for non-Claude providers. -->

CLAUDE.md was not found at project root. AIWG.md normally mirrors that content.
See [.aiwg/AIWG.md](.aiwg/AIWG.md) for the project framework context.

<!-- AIWG-PARALLELISM-CAP:START -->
## Parallelism Cap

This project caps parallel agent fan-out (#1359):

- **max_parallel_subagents**: 4 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_ralph_loops**: 2 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_mc_missions**: 4 (provider default for claude)

*Rationale*: Provider default for claude — adjust via 'aiwg config set --project parallelism.max_parallel_subagents N'

### Model-selected delegation rubric

For each non-trivial task, assess whether it contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. When delegation is supported, prefer the deployed model-pinned wrappers by task characteristics and consequence:

- `aiwg-model-efficiency-worker`: discovery, inventory, focused edits, and other bounded low-cost work.
- `aiwg-model-coding-worker`: implementation, tests, debugging, and routine technical delivery.
- `aiwg-model-reasoning-worker`: architecture, synthesis, difficult analysis, and high-consequence review.

Supplementary Specification (Non-Functional Requirements)

# Supplementary Specification (Non-Functional Requirements)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `requirements/supplementary-spec-template.md` |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Conventions", "Testing", "Verification", "Limits and next steps"), ADRs 0002, 0004, 0021, 0034, bug ledger, `UPSTREAM.md` |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

Numbered, testable statements with what verifies each ("—" = no automated check). `AGENTS.md` and the ADRs are authoritative. "Nightly" checks report, they don't block merges.

## Reliability

| ID | Requirement | Source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-REL-001 | No template, stylesheet, Fluent bundle or Markdown page makes the library panic or overflow the stack | ADR 0004, bug ledger | `tests/arbtest.rs` (`arbitrary_*_never_panics`), `tests/fuzz_corpus.rs` (replays), cargo-fuzz `css`/`html`/`ftl` (nightly, 15 min each), honggfuzz, fuzzcheck |
| NFR-REL-002 | A stylesheet that fails to load leaves an unstyled, working UI and recovers when it loads | bug_0001, bug_0004 | `tests/stateful.rs` (proptest-stateful) |
| NFR-REL-003 | A template render failure shows the error and recovers on the next good render | `AGENTS.md` Verification | `html_ui::template_render_failure_shows_the_error_and_recovers` |
| NFR-REL-004 | Correctness never depends on unspecified system order | `AGENTS.md` Verification | every `cargo test` run shuffles schedule order (`shuffle_seed`, `tests/common`) |
| NFR-REL-005 | Interaction signals follow the documented semantics for any page and pointer sequence | ADR 0006, 0011 | `tests/signal_properties.rs` (reference model), `tests/signals.rs` |
| NFR-REL-006 | A windowed build shows the same UI as an unwindowed one, except the one documented frame | ADR 0031–0033, bug_0170 | `tests/windowing_model.rs` |

## Conformance

| ID | Requirement | Source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-CONF-001 | Computed styles (font, size, color, box widths, border-image) match Chromium for every plain-HTML vector | ADR 0004 | `browser_oracle` (`tests/vectors/*/browser.json`); nightly re-checks against current Chrome |
| NFR-CONF-002 | Layout boxes match Chromium's within 1px | ADR 0004, 0007 | `layout_oracle` (`tests/vectors/layout_*`) |
| NFR-CONF-006 | Selectors match as lightningcss parsed them, with spec specificity (`:where()` zero, `:is()` its most specific argument); `:nth-child(0)` matches nothing | ADR 0034 | `browser_oracle` on `tests/vectors/selectors_level4`; `nth_child_zero_matches_no_element`; `tests/selector_model.rs` (Level 4 grammar) |
| NFR-CONF-003 | Localized output equals `@fluent/dom`'s for the same inputs | ADR 0004, 0013 | `fluent_oracle`; CI checks `fluent.html` is what `scripts/fluent_oracle.sh` produces |
| NFR-CONF-004 | Rendered pixels match the golden references on lavapipe (≤0.05 % differing pixels) | `AGENTS.md` Testing | `tests/golden.rs` (nightly) |
| NFR-CONF-005 | Every CSS deviation from the web is a documented limit and logs the skipped value at `debug` | `AGENTS.md` Limits | — (convention) |

## Performance

| ID | Requirement | Source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-PERF-001 | Unchanged subtrees skip the cascade, spec construction and diff (600-element change: ≈1.2 ms vs ≈2.1 ms without) | ADR 0021 | `benches/pipeline.rs` (criterion), `benches/pipeline-divan.rs` (nightly) |
| NFR-PERF-002 | Updates write a kept element's components only where they differ (change ticks preserved) | ADR 0009 | test vectors (`tests/html_ui.rs`) |
| NFR-PERF-003 | Hot pipeline functions don't regress beyond the hotpath policy | `AGENTS.md` Public API | `hotpath/policy.toml` |

## Supportability

| ID | Requirement | Source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-SUP-001 | The library builds warning-free with its minimal Bevy features, and with `text-input` | ADR 0002 | CI: `cargo check --lib` (both), `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings` |
| NFR-SUP-002 | Rustdoc is warning-free and doc examples compile | `AGENTS.md` Conventions | CI: `cargo doc --no-deps`, doctests |
| NFR-SUP-003 | Every user-visible change has a `CHANGELOG.md` line under `[Unreleased]` | `AGENTS.md` Conventions | — (convention) |
| NFR-SUP-004 | Every example template renders in every locale and context, with no untranslated text | `AGENTS.md` Testing | `tests/content_lint.rs` (`every_template_is_listed` keeps it complete) |
| NFR-SUP-005 | Library code has no debug prints and writes no files | `AGENTS.md` | `source_lint::library_code_has_no_debug_prints`, `library_code_writes_no_files` |
| NFR-SUP-006 | Every defect gets a bug report and a regression test when its fix lands | `AGENTS.md` Bug reports | — (convention; ledger in `docs/agents/bugs/INDEX.md`) |

## Security

| ID | Requirement | Source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-SEC-001 | Template input is treated as untrusted: a panic reachable from user data is high severity | `AGENTS.md` Bug reports | fuzzing (NFR-REL-001) |
| NFR-SEC-002 | Tera autoescaping round-trips; entities are decoded one level only | `AGENTS.md` Testing | `template.rs` unit tests and proptest |
| NFR-SEC-005 | Selector forms parcel's matcher panics on (`:nth-child(… of S)`, `:has()`, `&` nesting, `:nth-col()`) never reach it: the allowlist skips their rules | ADR 0034 | `cascade::tests::the_engine_allowlist`; the testbench's selector-engine scenario |
| NFR-SEC-003 | Known upstream panics are patched locally until fixed upstream, and apps are told to apply the patch | `UPSTREAM.md` U1, U2 | `[patch.crates-io]` in `Cargo.toml`; README section |
| NFR-SEC-004 | The `dev-tools` surface (localhost BRP + MCP) is never enabled in a shipped build | `Cargo.toml` features | — (opt-in feature) |

## Design Constraints

| ID | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| NFR-DES-001 | Bevy 0.20; the library maps HTML/CSS/Fluent/Tera to Bevy UI and nothing else; app decisions (panels, input bindings, fonts, asset paths) stay in apps | ADR 0002 |
| NFR-DES-002 | Global configuration is resources; per-entity configuration is components; public items go in the prelude | `AGENTS.md` Conventions |
| NFR-DES-003 | When to update is decided by the pure `rebuild` state machine, unit-tested in `rebuild::tests` | ADR 0005 |

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0002-library-shape-and-public-api.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0004-verification-strategy.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0005-update-decisions-as-a-pure-state-machine.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0009-in-place-update-model.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0021-per-element-dirty-tracking.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0031-windowed-build-spec-level-culling.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0034-match-selectors-with-parcel-selectors.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/bug_0001.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/bug_0170.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/UPSTREAM.md

Chain of Custody Log

# Chain of Custody Log

> This document records the collection, transfer, and storage of all evidence for the referenced case.
> Every person who handles evidence MUST log a transfer entry. Gaps in custody chain may compromise
> the admissibility of evidence. Complete all fields — do not leave entries blank.

---

## Case Information

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Case ID | `{{case_id}}` |
| Case Title | `{{case_title}}` |
| Target System | `{{hostname}}` |
| Investigation Date | `{{investigation_date}}` |
| Lead Investigator | `{{investigator_name}}` |
| Authorized By | `{{authorized_by}}` |
| Authorization Reference | `{{authorization_ref}}` |
| Classification | `{{classification}}` |
| This Document Version | `{{doc_version}}` |
| Last Updated | `{{last_updated}}` |

---

## Evidence Item Register

Each distinct piece of evidence collected during this investigation. Assign a unique ID (E-001, E-002, etc.) to each item at time of collection. Never reuse IDs within a case.

| ID | Description | Source Path / Location | Collection Date/Time | Hash Algorithm | Hash Value | Collected By | Integrity Verified |
|----|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| E-001 | `{{evidence_desc_1}}` | `{{source_path_1}}` | `{{collection_datetime_1}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_1}}` | `{{collector_1}}` | `{{verified_1}}` |
| E-002 | `{{evidence_desc_2}}` | `{{source_path_2}}` | `{{collection_datetime_2}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_2}}` | `{{collector_2}}` | `{{verified_2}}` |
| E-003 | `{{evidence_desc_3}}` | `{{source_path_3}}` | `{{collection_datetime_3}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_3}}` | `{{collector_3}}` | `{{verified_3}}` |

### Collection Notes

```
{{collection_notes}}
```

### Packet Evidence Bundle Entries (optional)

Add one row when a validated `PacketEvidenceBundle` enters the case. This is an
additive register; existing evidence rows remain valid.

| Evidence ID | Bundle ID | Capture SHA-256 | Bundle Status | TShark Path / Version | Analysis Context / Filter Digest | Received UTC / From / By | Storage | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-XXX | `packet-evidence:...` | `sha256:...` | completed / partial / empty | `/absolute/tshark` / `x.y.z` | `sha256:...` / `sha256:...` | `...` | `...` | `...` |

Keep the full command argv, config digests, derived-artifact hashes, and stable
frame/stream locators in the machine-readable manifest entry. Raw payload stays
withheld unless an explicit case policy permits it.

### Evidence Inventory Commands Used

```bash
# Hash all files in evidence directory at collection time
find /evidence/{{case_id}} -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256

# Verify hashes later (run to confirm no tampering)
sha256sum -c /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256
```

---

## Custody Transfer Log

Record every transfer of evidence between individuals or storage locations. A transfer occurs any time evidence moves from one person's control, or from one storage location, to another.

| Transfer ID | Date / Time | From (Name / Location) | To (Name / Location) | Purpose | Evidence Items | Signature / Confirmation |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------|---------------|-------------------------|
| T-001 | `{{transfer_datetime_1}}` | `{{from_1}}` | `{{to_1}}` | `{{purpose_1}}` | `{{items_1}}` | `{{signature_1}}` |
| T-002 | `{{transfer_datetime_2}}` | `{{from_2}}` | `{{to_2}}` | `{{purpose_2}}` | `{{items_2}}` | `{{signature_2}}` |
| T-003 | `{{transfer_datetime_3}}` | `{{from_3}}` | `{{to_3}}` | `{{purpose_3}}` | `{{items_3}}` | `{{signature_3}}` |

**Transfer Protocol:**

- Confirm hash values match before and after any transfer involving digital media
- Both parties must acknowledge the transfer in writing (or via tracked ticketing system)
- Physical media transfers require secure packaging and a transport manifest
- Remote transfers (e.g., SCP, SFTP) must use encrypted channels; log source and destination IPs

---

## Evidence Integrity Verification

Record results of integrity checks performed after collection and after each transfer. A failed check requires immediate escalation — do not continue using the evidence until the discrepancy is resolved.

| Check ID | Date / Time | Evidence Item(s) | Expected Hash | Computed Hash | Result | Performed By | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-----------------|--------------|--------------|--------|-------------|-------|
| IC-001 | `{{check_datetime_1}}` | `{{check_items_1}}` | `{{expected_hash_1}}` | `{{computed_hash_1}}` | `{{result_1}}` | `{{checker_1}}` | `{{check_notes_1}}` |
| IC-002 | `{{check_datetime_2}}` | `{{check_items_2}}` | `{{expected_hash_2}}` | `{{computed_hash_2}}` | `{{result_2}}` | `{{checker_2}}` | `{{check_notes_2}}` |

**Integrity Failure Protocol:**

If a hash mismatch is detected:

1. Immediately quarantine the affected evidence item.
2. Document the discrepancy in this log (do not alter or delete the mismatched entry).
3. Notify `{{integrity_escalation_contact}}`.
4. Do not use the affected evidence in the investigation until the source of the mismatch is determined.
5. If the original source system is still accessible, re-collect the affected item and restart its custody chain.

---

## Storage Location

| Period | Location | Access Control | Custodian |
|--------|----------|---------------|-----------|
| Active investigation | `{{active_storage_path}}` | `{{active_access_control}}` | `{{active_custodian}}` |
| Post-investigation archive | `{{archive_storage_path}}` | `{{archive_access_control}}` | `{{archive_custodian}}` |
| Offsite backup (if applicable) | `{{offsite_storage_path}}` | `{{offsite_access_control}}` | `{{offsite_custodian}}` |

**Retention Period:** `{{retention_period}}`

**Destruction Authorization:** Evidence may only be destroyed after written authorization from `{{destruction_authority}}` and not before `{{earliest_destruction_date}}`.

---

```
{{general_notes}}
```

---

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
|---------|------|--------|---------|
| 1.0 | `{{doc_creation_date}}` | `{{investigator_name}}` | Initial document |
| `{{version_2}}` | `{{date_2}}` | `{{author_2}}` | `{{changes_2}}` |

.aiwg/frameworks/forensics-complete/chain-of-custody.md
> This document records the collection, transfer, and storage of all evidence for the referenced case. > Every person who handles evidence MUST log a transfer entry. Gaps in custody chain may compromise > the admissibility of evidence. Complete all fields — do not leave entries blank. --- | Field | Value |
Chain of Custody Log

# Chain of Custody Log

> This document records the collection, transfer, and storage of all evidence for the referenced case.
> Every person who handles evidence MUST log a transfer entry. Gaps in custody chain may compromise
> the admissibility of evidence. Complete all fields — do not leave entries blank.

---

## Case Information

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Case ID | `{{case_id}}` |
| Case Title | `{{case_title}}` |
| Target System | `{{hostname}}` |
| Investigation Date | `{{investigation_date}}` |
| Lead Investigator | `{{investigator_name}}` |
| Authorized By | `{{authorized_by}}` |
| Authorization Reference | `{{authorization_ref}}` |
| Classification | `{{classification}}` |
| This Document Version | `{{doc_version}}` |
| Last Updated | `{{last_updated}}` |

---

## Evidence Item Register

Each distinct piece of evidence collected during this investigation. Assign a unique ID (E-001, E-002, etc.) to each item at time of collection. Never reuse IDs within a case.

| ID | Description | Source Path / Location | Collection Date/Time | Hash Algorithm | Hash Value | Collected By | Integrity Verified |
|----|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| E-001 | `{{evidence_desc_1}}` | `{{source_path_1}}` | `{{collection_datetime_1}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_1}}` | `{{collector_1}}` | `{{verified_1}}` |
| E-002 | `{{evidence_desc_2}}` | `{{source_path_2}}` | `{{collection_datetime_2}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_2}}` | `{{collector_2}}` | `{{verified_2}}` |
| E-003 | `{{evidence_desc_3}}` | `{{source_path_3}}` | `{{collection_datetime_3}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_3}}` | `{{collector_3}}` | `{{verified_3}}` |

### Collection Notes

```
{{collection_notes}}
```

### Packet Evidence Bundle Entries (optional)

Add one row when a validated `PacketEvidenceBundle` enters the case. This is an
additive register; existing evidence rows remain valid.

| Evidence ID | Bundle ID | Capture SHA-256 | Bundle Status | TShark Path / Version | Analysis Context / Filter Digest | Received UTC / From / By | Storage | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-XXX | `packet-evidence:...` | `sha256:...` | completed / partial / empty | `/absolute/tshark` / `x.y.z` | `sha256:...` / `sha256:...` | `...` | `...` | `...` |

Keep the full command argv, config digests, derived-artifact hashes, and stable
frame/stream locators in the machine-readable manifest entry. Raw payload stays
withheld unless an explicit case policy permits it.

### Evidence Inventory Commands Used

```bash
# Hash all files in evidence directory at collection time
find /evidence/{{case_id}} -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256

# Verify hashes later (run to confirm no tampering)
sha256sum -c /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256
```

---

## Custody Transfer Log

Record every transfer of evidence between individuals or storage locations. A transfer occurs any time evidence moves from one person's control, or from one storage location, to another.

| Transfer ID | Date / Time | From (Name / Location) | To (Name / Location) | Purpose | Evidence Items | Signature / Confirmation |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------|---------------|-------------------------|
| T-001 | `{{transfer_datetime_1}}` | `{{from_1}}` | `{{to_1}}` | `{{purpose_1}}` | `{{items_1}}` | `{{signature_1}}` |
| T-002 | `{{transfer_datetime_2}}` | `{{from_2}}` | `{{to_2}}` | `{{purpose_2}}` | `{{items_2}}` | `{{signature_2}}` |
| T-003 | `{{transfer_datetime_3}}` | `{{from_3}}` | `{{to_3}}` | `{{purpose_3}}` | `{{items_3}}` | `{{signature_3}}` |

**Transfer Protocol:**

- Confirm hash values match before and after any transfer involving digital media
- Both parties must acknowledge the transfer in writing (or via tracked ticketing system)
- Physical media transfers require secure packaging and a transport manifest
- Remote transfers (e.g., SCP, SFTP) must use encrypted channels; log source and destination IPs

---

## Evidence Integrity Verification

Record results of integrity checks performed after collection and after each transfer. A failed check requires immediate escalation — do not continue using the evidence until the discrepancy is resolved.

| Check ID | Date / Time | Evidence Item(s) | Expected Hash | Computed Hash | Result | Performed By | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-----------------|--------------|--------------|--------|-------------|-------|
| IC-001 | `{{check_datetime_1}}` | `{{check_items_1}}` | `{{expected_hash_1}}` | `{{computed_hash_1}}` | `{{result_1}}` | `{{checker_1}}` | `{{check_notes_1}}` |
| IC-002 | `{{check_datetime_2}}` | `{{check_items_2}}` | `{{expected_hash_2}}` | `{{computed_hash_2}}` | `{{result_2}}` | `{{checker_2}}` | `{{check_notes_2}}` |

**Integrity Failure Protocol:**

If a hash mismatch is detected:

1. Immediately quarantine the affected evidence item.
2. Document the discrepancy in this log (do not alter or delete the mismatched entry).
3. Notify `{{integrity_escalation_contact}}`.
4. Do not use the affected evidence in the investigation until the source of the mismatch is determined.
5. If the original source system is still accessible, re-collect the affected item and restart its custody chain.

---

## Storage Location

| Period | Location | Access Control | Custodian |
|--------|----------|---------------|-----------|
| Active investigation | `{{active_storage_path}}` | `{{active_access_control}}` | `{{active_custodian}}` |
| Post-investigation archive | `{{archive_storage_path}}` | `{{archive_access_control}}` | `{{archive_custodian}}` |
| Offsite backup (if applicable) | `{{offsite_storage_path}}` | `{{offsite_access_control}}` | `{{offsite_custodian}}` |

**Retention Period:** `{{retention_period}}`

**Destruction Authorization:** Evidence may only be destroyed after written authorization from `{{destruction_authority}}` and not before `{{earliest_destruction_date}}`.

---

## Notes

```
{{general_notes}}
```

---

## Document Control

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
|---------|------|--------|---------|
| 1.0 | `{{doc_creation_date}}` | `{{investigator_name}}` | Initial document |
| `{{version_2}}` | `{{date_2}}` | `{{author_2}}` | `{{changes_2}}` |

.aiwg/requirements/use-cases.md
| Field | Value | |---|---| | Template | `requirements/use-case-brief-template.md` (one brief per section) | | Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Public API", "Limits and next steps", "Verification"), ADRs 0001–0034, examples | | Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |
Use-Case Briefs

# Use-Case Briefs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `requirements/use-case-brief-template.md` (one brief per section) |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Public API", "Limits and next steps", "Verification"), ADRs 0001–0034, examples |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

Status: **Built** or **Planned**. IDs are stable. Each brief names the example that exercises it (`cargo run --example <name>`).

## Actors

| Actor | Who |
|---|---|
| Developer | Bevy app developer adding `BevyMarkupPlugin` |
| Author | Writes templates, stylesheets and Markdown pages |
| Translator | Writes Fluent (`.ftl.ron`) bundles |
| Player | End user of the game or app, with mouse, touch, keyboard or gamepad |
| Agent | AI coding agent using the `dev-tools` QA surface |

## Built

### UC-001 — Developer shows a template as Bevy UI

- **Main success scenario:** spawn `HtmlUi(template)` with a `TemplateContext`; the pipeline renders, parses, localizes, cascades and builds native UI entities; mutating the context re-renders and rebuilds only if the HTML changed.
- **Notes:** `RenderedHtml` exposes `Pending`/`Ready`/`Failed`; a render failure shows the error and recovers. Example: `quickstart`. Sources: ADR 0001, 0002, 0005.

### UC-002 — Author styles and lays out UI with CSS

- **Main success scenario:** a stylesheet (per entity or `DefaultStylesheet`) styles elements through the cascade; flex, grid (named lines and areas), positioning and `calc()` lay them out; `border-image` draws 9-slice frames; swapping the default sheet changes theme.
- **Notes:** the supported subset and its deviations are documented limits, each skipped value logged at `debug`. Selectors are lightningcss's parse matched by its engine (ADR 0034): `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` lists, `:nth-last-*`, `:only-*` and attribute operators on `data-*` work; an unsupported selector skips its rule. Examples: `grid`, `grid-names`, `calc`, `combinators`, `demo`. Sources: ADR 0003, 0007, 0027, 0028, 0030, 0034.

### UC-003 — Translator localizes the UI

- **Main success scenario:** elements carry `data-l10n-id` (and `data-l10n-args`); setting `ActiveLocale` translates them, with plurals and `data-l10n-name` overlays; swapping it changes language at runtime.
- **Notes:** numbers format without locale grouping. Examples: `demo`, `menu`. Sources: ADR 0013, bug_0006, bug_0007.

### UC-004 — Author writes pages in Markdown

- **Main success scenario:** a `.md` template is converted to HTML at load (pulldown-cmark) and styled like any template.
- **Notes:** indentation inside Tera blocks or HTML containers is not Markdown; indented code blocks are disabled. Example: `markdown`. Sources: ADR 0014, 0020, 0024–0026.

### UC-005 — Player interacts with the UI

- **Main success scenario:** `data-on-<trigger>` elements emit `ElementSignal`s on click, press, release, enter and leave (the deepest bound element wins); `:hover`/`:active` restyle in place; the app reacts by reading the messages or routing by name (`on_html_click`).
- **Notes:** forms emit a `Submit` signal with the named inputs' values. Examples: `menu`, `forms`, `links`. Sources: ADR 0006, 0011.

### UC-006 — Player navigates with keyboard or gamepad

- **Main success scenario:** the app binds its own input to `HtmlFocus::navigate` (compass directions) and `activate`; focus moves between focusable elements, `:focus-visible` shows it, activation emits the element's click signals; `HtmlModal` confines focus.
- **Notes:** no Tab order (directional only). Example: `menu`. Source: ADR 0008.

### UC-007 — App updates the UI in place

- **Main success scenario:** a context, locale or stylesheet change updates the existing entity tree: identical renders are skipped, elements are matched by `id` or position, unchanged subtrees are reused, style-only changes restyle in place; `HtmlUiBuilt`/`HtmlUiRestyled` report what happened.
- **Notes:** app components attached to kept elements survive; handlers on `HtmlUiBuilt` must be idempotent. Example: `live`. Sources: ADR 0009, 0017, 0021, 0029.

### UC-008 — Developer shows overlays and tooltips

- **Main success scenario:** `data-tooltip` shows a tooltip template beside the hovered element; `HtmlAnchor` keeps an overlay beside an element; `HtmlWorldAnchor` keeps a UI root over a 3D entity.
- **Example:** `world`. Source: ADR 0010.

### UC-009 — Developer attaches app behaviour to elements

- **Main success scenario:** `define_html_element(name, system)` runs the app's system for every spawned `is="<name>"` element with its `data-*` dataset; `HtmlElements` finds elements by id, class or tag.
- **Example:** `inputs`. Source: ADR 0012.

### UC-010 — Player types into a text field

- **Main success scenario:** with the `text-input` feature, `<input type="text">` becomes Bevy's editable text widget; `maxlength` limits characters; the form's submit collects the values.
- **Notes:** single-line only, no `placeholder`. Examples: `forms`, `inputs`. Sources: ADR 0016, 0022, 0023.

### UC-011 — Developer shows a long scrolling document

- **Main success scenario:** a long list in a scroll container builds only the rows in and near the visible band; scrolling builds the newly visible rows.
- **Notes:** a height change above the band can misplace rows for one frame (bug_0170, won't fix). Sources: ADR 0031–0033.

### UC-012 — Author edits assets with hot reload

- **Main success scenario:** with the `hot-reload` feature, editing a template, stylesheet or bundle on disk updates the running UI.
- **Example:** `hot-reload`. Source: `AGENTS.md` Conventions.

### UC-013 — Agent playtests an example

- **Main success scenario:** run an example with `--features dev-tools`; over localhost BRP/MCP the agent reads the UI tree, clicks nodes, mocks keyboard/gamepad/mouse input, asserts and takes screenshots.
- **Notes:** dev only, never in a shipped build. Source: `AGENTS.md` Verification.

## Planned (ADR 0028 tier 4)

### UC-101 — Author uses SVG images

- **Status:** open. Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-102 — Author writes responsive CSS with `@media`

- **Status:** open. Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-103 — Author uses shadows and gradients

- **Status:** open (`box-shadow`, `text-shadow`, gradients as images). Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-104 — Author animates with `@keyframes`

- **Status:** open; must fit the rebuild model. Source: ADR 0028.

Deferred until Bevy offers the capability: `position: sticky`, `<textarea>`, built-in checkbox/radio (ADR 0028).

- @docs/agents/adr/0001-html-tera-fluent-css-onto-bevy-ui.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0006-declarative-interaction-signals-and-pseudo-classes.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0008-focus-and-navigation-in-the-library.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0009-in-place-update-model.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0010-overlays-anchors-and-tooltips.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0012-template-composition-and-examples.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0013-own-the-fluent-bundle-asset.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0016-text-input.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0021-per-element-dirty-tracking.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0028-modern-authoring-gaps-roadmap.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0032-windowed-build-revised.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0034-match-selectors-with-parcel-selectors.md
- @examples/README.md

Use-Case Briefs

# Use-Case Briefs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `requirements/use-case-brief-template.md` (one brief per section) |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Public API", "Limits and next steps", "Verification"), ADRs 0001–0034, examples |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

Status: **Built** or **Planned**. IDs are stable. Each brief names the example that exercises it (`cargo run --example <name>`).

## Actors

| Actor | Who |
|---|---|
| Developer | Bevy app developer adding `BevyMarkupPlugin` |
| Author | Writes templates, stylesheets and Markdown pages |
| Translator | Writes Fluent (`.ftl.ron`) bundles |
| Player | End user of the game or app, with mouse, touch, keyboard or gamepad |
| Agent | AI coding agent using the `dev-tools` QA surface |

## Built

### UC-001 — Developer shows a template as Bevy UI

- **Main success scenario:** spawn `HtmlUi(template)` with a `TemplateContext`; the pipeline renders, parses, localizes, cascades and builds native UI entities; mutating the context re-renders and rebuilds only if the HTML changed.
- **Notes:** `RenderedHtml` exposes `Pending`/`Ready`/`Failed`; a render failure shows the error and recovers. Example: `quickstart`. Sources: ADR 0001, 0002, 0005.

### UC-002 — Author styles and lays out UI with CSS

- **Main success scenario:** a stylesheet (per entity or `DefaultStylesheet`) styles elements through the cascade; flex, grid (named lines and areas), positioning and `calc()` lay them out; `border-image` draws 9-slice frames; swapping the default sheet changes theme.
- **Notes:** the supported subset and its deviations are documented limits, each skipped value logged at `debug`. Selectors are lightningcss's parse matched by its engine (ADR 0034): `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` lists, `:nth-last-*`, `:only-*` and attribute operators on `data-*` work; an unsupported selector skips its rule. Examples: `grid`, `grid-names`, `calc`, `combinators`, `demo`. Sources: ADR 0003, 0007, 0027, 0028, 0030, 0034.

### UC-003 — Translator localizes the UI

- **Main success scenario:** elements carry `data-l10n-id` (and `data-l10n-args`); setting `ActiveLocale` translates them, with plurals and `data-l10n-name` overlays; swapping it changes language at runtime.
- **Notes:** numbers format without locale grouping. Examples: `demo`, `menu`. Sources: ADR 0013, bug_0006, bug_0007.

### UC-004 — Author writes pages in Markdown

- **Main success scenario:** a `.md` template is converted to HTML at load (pulldown-cmark) and styled like any template.
- **Notes:** indentation inside Tera blocks or HTML containers is not Markdown; indented code blocks are disabled. Example: `markdown`. Sources: ADR 0014, 0020, 0024–0026.

### UC-005 — Player interacts with the UI

- **Main success scenario:** `data-on-<trigger>` elements emit `ElementSignal`s on click, press, release, enter and leave (the deepest bound element wins); `:hover`/`:active` restyle in place; the app reacts by reading the messages or routing by name (`on_html_click`).
- **Notes:** forms emit a `Submit` signal with the named inputs' values. Examples: `menu`, `forms`, `links`. Sources: ADR 0006, 0011.

### UC-006 — Player navigates with keyboard or gamepad

- **Main success scenario:** the app binds its own input to `HtmlFocus::navigate` (compass directions) and `activate`; focus moves between focusable elements, `:focus-visible` shows it, activation emits the element's click signals; `HtmlModal` confines focus.
- **Notes:** no Tab order (directional only). Example: `menu`. Source: ADR 0008.

### UC-007 — App updates the UI in place

- **Main success scenario:** a context, locale or stylesheet change updates the existing entity tree: identical renders are skipped, elements are matched by `id` or position, unchanged subtrees are reused, style-only changes restyle in place; `HtmlUiBuilt`/`HtmlUiRestyled` report what happened.
- **Notes:** app components attached to kept elements survive; handlers on `HtmlUiBuilt` must be idempotent. Example: `live`. Sources: ADR 0009, 0017, 0021, 0029.

### UC-008 — Developer shows overlays and tooltips

- **Main success scenario:** `data-tooltip` shows a tooltip template beside the hovered element; `HtmlAnchor` keeps an overlay beside an element; `HtmlWorldAnchor` keeps a UI root over a 3D entity.
- **Example:** `world`. Source: ADR 0010.

### UC-009 — Developer attaches app behaviour to elements

- **Main success scenario:** `define_html_element(name, system)` runs the app's system for every spawned `is="<name>"` element with its `data-*` dataset; `HtmlElements` finds elements by id, class or tag.
- **Example:** `inputs`. Source: ADR 0012.

### UC-010 — Player types into a text field

- **Main success scenario:** with the `text-input` feature, `<input type="text">` becomes Bevy's editable text widget; `maxlength` limits characters; the form's submit collects the values.
- **Notes:** single-line only, no `placeholder`. Examples: `forms`, `inputs`. Sources: ADR 0016, 0022, 0023.

### UC-011 — Developer shows a long scrolling document

- **Main success scenario:** a long list in a scroll container builds only the rows in and near the visible band; scrolling builds the newly visible rows.
- **Notes:** a height change above the band can misplace rows for one frame (bug_0170, won't fix). Sources: ADR 0031–0033.

### UC-012 — Author edits assets with hot reload

- **Main success scenario:** with the `hot-reload` feature, editing a template, stylesheet or bundle on disk updates the running UI.
- **Example:** `hot-reload`. Source: `AGENTS.md` Conventions.

### UC-013 — Agent playtests an example

- **Main success scenario:** run an example with `--features dev-tools`; over localhost BRP/MCP the agent reads the UI tree, clicks nodes, mocks keyboard/gamepad/mouse input, asserts and takes screenshots.
- **Notes:** dev only, never in a shipped build. Source: `AGENTS.md` Verification.

## Planned (ADR 0028 tier 4)

### UC-101 — Author uses SVG images

- **Status:** open. Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-102 — Author writes responsive CSS with `@media`

- **Status:** open. Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-103 — Author uses shadows and gradients

- **Status:** open (`box-shadow`, `text-shadow`, gradients as images). Source: ADR 0028.

### UC-104 — Author animates with `@keyframes`

- **Status:** open; must fit the rebuild model. Source: ADR 0028.

Deferred until Bevy offers the capability: `position: sticky`, `<textarea>`, built-in checkbox/radio (ADR 0028).

# AIWG.md
<!-- aiwg-managed -->
<!-- Normalized project-local AIWG context. Operator notes may live outside AIWG-managed blocks. -->

This file is the stable `.aiwg/AIWG.md` entry point for AIWG skills, rules, and generated provider context.

<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:START -->
## Context Finalization

This section is synthesized after template emission from the current workspace state. Preserve operator-authored content outside AIWG-managed blocks; rerun `aiwg regenerate` to refresh this section after provider, framework, or MCP wiring changes.

### Workspace Snapshot

- Configured providers: claude
- Installed frameworks/addons: all
- Recorded deployments: claude
- Normalized project context: `.aiwg/AIWG.md`

### Discover-First Protocol

Classify every user turn FIRST: is it a **new directive** or a continuation? When a message names or references an AIWG command/capability — even as pasted content like an `address-issues` tracker table, an issue list, or a `flow-*` name — treat it as a new directive and ACT: run `aiwg discover "<the need>"`, fetch with `aiwg show <type> <name>`, and invoke it. Do NOT ask "what would you like me to do with these?" when the action is implied — a pasted `address-issues #1234` table means run the address-issues workflow on those issues.

Also run `aiwg discover` before declining an AIWG request as out of scope or inventing a workflow from memory. The CLI ranks AIWG capabilities across the installed corpus and rebuilds the index from `$AIWG_ROOT` automatically, so a "no matches" for a command you know is deployed is a bug — not a signal it is absent. Commands AIWG deploys to your provider command directory (`.opencode/command/`, `.claude/commands/`, `~/.codex/prompts/`, …) ARE discoverable this way; fetch them with `aiwg show command <name>`. This prevents decline-without-search failures, ask-instead-of-act on new directives, and hallucinated skill or agent names. Full rule: `agentic/code/addons/aiwg-utils/rules/skill-discovery.md`.

### Engagement Verification

When a user asks whether AIWG is active or engaged in this project, run or read `aiwg status --probe --json` and report the result plainly: engaged state, project root, deployed provider files, installed frameworks/addons, and the next action from the probe. Do not add AIWG attribution, signatures, generated-by text, or passive footers to user files, commits, PRs, comments, code headers, or docs.

### Tracker Authority Protocol

- Source of truth: [.aiwg/aiwg.config](./aiwg.config)
- Internal/canonical tracker: `origin` (github; git@github.com:nchashch/bevy_markup.git)
- Customer issue tracker: not configured
- Primary repo remote: `origin`; CI remote: `origin`
- Secondary/mirror remotes: none configured
- Issue storage mode: not configured

Tracker access order for issue, PR, release, and CI-sensitive tracker operations:
1. MCP/app tools for the configured tracker.
2. Tracker HTTP API with configured credentials.
3. Tracker CLI for the configured tracker, after confirming authentication.
4. Stop and report a blocker.

- Project config decides tracker authority; installed/authenticated CLIs do not.
- Route internal engineering, delivery, and CI-sensitive issue work to the internal tracker.
- Route customer acknowledgements, follow-up, and closure to the customer tracker when configured.
- Git SSH remote access is repository sync, not issue-tracker API access.
- Do not file on mirror or secondary remotes just because their CLI is authenticated.
- Treat an unauthenticated tracker CLI as one failed access path, then continue probing MCP/app/API before blocking.

### Source Model

- `.aiwg/AIWG.md` is the normalized project-local context entry point.
- Root `AIWG.md` is the generated cross-provider companion loaded through `AGENTS.md` and provider twins.
- `AGENTS.md`, `WARP.md`, `.hermes.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` are provider-facing bridges, not replacements for `.aiwg/AIWG.md`.
<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:END -->

Option Matrix (Project Context and Priorities)

# Option Matrix (Project Context and Priorities)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0001, 0002, 0004, 0028 |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |

## Project Reality

- A library, not an app: its users are Bevy developers and template authors; its end users are the players of those games.
- One developer with AI agents; verification is the method that lets agents change it safely (ADR 0004).
- Consumers inside the studio: prototype_19, vtuber; published on crates.io.

## Priorities (weights sum to 10)

| Priority | Weight | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fidelity to web semantics (what an author expects from HTML/CSS/Fluent) | 3 | oracles against Chromium and `@fluent/dom`; deviations are documented limits |
| Robustness against any input | 3 | untrusted-input stance; fuzzers; "reachable from user data = high" |
| Small surface and dependency set | 2 | ADR 0002; minimal Bevy features; app decisions stay in apps |
| Update performance | 2 | ADR 0009, 0021, 0031; benchmark suites |

## Trade-offs Already Made

- Bevy's capabilities bound the subset: no sticky positioning, no inline boxes with content, no multi-line text input (ADR 0028).
- `flex-shrink: 0` default kept for compatibility with existing layouts, against CSS (open question).
- Application input bindings stay in apps; the library offers `HtmlFocus` instead (ADR 0008).

| Update performance | 2 | ADR 0009, 0021, 0031; benchmark suites |

## Trade-offs Already Made

- Bevy's capabilities bound the subset: no sticky positioning, no inline boxes with content, no multi-line text input (ADR 0028).
- `flex-shrink: 0` default kept for compatibility with existing layouts, against CSS (open question).
- Application input bindings stay in apps; the library offers `HtmlFocus` instead (ADR 0008).

# SDLC Index — bevy_markup

_Generated: 2026-10-28 — 9 pages · consumer `sdlc-complete` · workspace `noetic-basho-technologies` (root: `../aiwg`)_

Derived pages cite their sources with `@path` mentions; provenance records are in `.aiwg/research/provenance/records/`. Authoritative: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/adr/`, `docs/agents/bugs/`, `docs/agents/reviews/`, `docs/agents/skills/`.

## Intake (3)
- [Project intake](intake/project-intake.md) — HTML/Tera + CSS + Fluent → Bevy UI library; 0.7.0 on crates.io; UI layer of prototype_19 and vtuber
- [Solution profile](intake/solution-profile.md) — published 0.x library; very strong verification, nightly red since 2026-10-14
- [Option matrix](intake/option-matrix.md) — priorities: web fidelity, robustness, small surface, update performance

## Requirements (2)
- [Use-case briefs](requirements/use-cases.md) — UC-001–013 built (templates, CSS, Fluent, Markdown, interaction, focus, updates, overlays, custom elements, text input, windowing, hot reload, agent QA); UC-101–104 planned (ADR 0028 tier 4)
- [Supplementary specification](requirements/supplementary-spec.md) — reliability, conformance (oracles), performance, supportability, security requirements with their checks (incl. ADR 0034's selector engine and allowlist)

## Risks (1)
- [Risk list](risks/risk-list.md) — R-001–008; highest: nightly red two weeks (fixed), fluent-syntax patch not reaching apps, silent CSS deviations, Bevy churn

## Testing (2)
- [Test strategy](testing/test-strategy.md) — unit, vectors, oracles, property/model tests, golden images, five fuzzers, mutants, coverage, benchmarks
- [Defect register](testing/defect-register.md) — bug_0001–0180: 178 fixed, none open; 15 upstream; nightly failures fixed (uncommitted)

## Architecture (1)
- [Architecture](architecture/README.md) — pointer to `AGENTS.md` and ADRs 0001–0034

Risk List

# Risk List

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `management/risk-list-template.md` |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0028, 0034, bug ledger, `UPSTREAM.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, CI history (GitHub Actions, 2026-10-28) |
| Source state | `cf0da55`, 2026-10-28 |
| Owner | Project owner (all risks) |

Scales High / Medium / Low; Exposure = Impact × Likelihood. Never renumber.

## Register

| Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Exposure | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-001 | The nightly workflow failed every night 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-28, so its findings went unseen (and timeouts masked a panic, bug_0180). Causes: two lightningcss defects and a vector without its Chrome reference (defect register). | High | High | HxH=High | Fixed (bug_0179, bug_0180, oracle script; merged to `main` 2026-10-28); keep the nightly green so a new failure is a signal, and triage a red night within days. | Owner | Mitigating | Low once green |
| R-002 | Two upstream fluent-syntax defects (panic, stack overflow from any FTL asset) are fixed only in a fork applied by `[patch.crates-io]`, which works only in the top-level project: apps without the same entry inherit them (both studio apps have it: prototype_19, and vtuber since 2026-10-28). | High | Medium | HxM=High | README asks apps to add the patch; get the upstream PRs merged (U1, U2), then drop the fork. | Owner | Mitigating | Low after upstream fix |
| R-003 | CSS copied from the web misbehaves silently where the subset deviates, notably `flex-shrink` defaulting to 0 (bug_0028); skipped values are logged only at `debug`. | Medium | High | MxH=High | Decide `flex-shrink` as a deliberate change (re-derive vectors against browser defaults); keep limits documented. | Owner | Open | Medium |
| R-004 | Releases lag `main`: a large `[Unreleased]` changelog since 0.7.0 (2026-10-15); prototype_19 still on 0.4.0, so its fixes and features don't reach the studio's game. | Medium | Medium | MxM=Medium | Release from `[Unreleased]`; bump prototype_19 (a migration across 0.5–0.7). | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-005 | Each Bevy release changes UI internals the library leans on (0.20's weakly ordered `UiSystems`, picking, text): migrations are large and can break subtly. | Medium | High | MxH=High | Schedule-order shuffling in every test run; oracles and golden images catch regressions; pin explicit ordering. | Owner | Accepted | Medium |
| R-006 | Golden images depend on the CI runner's Mesa (lavapipe is canonical; `ubuntu-latest` moved to Ubuntu 26 on 2026-10-19): a renderer change fails the job without a code change. | Low | Medium | LxM=Low | Re-record with the `Update golden references (lavapipe)` job; `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` as fallback. | Owner | Accepted | Low |
| R-007 | The repository lives on the personal `nchashch` account while the studio's other repositories are on the `noeticbasho` org. | Medium | Low | MxL=Low | Transfer to the org when convenient (crates.io `repository` field follows). | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-008 | `AGENTS.md` is ~130 KB; every agent session that loads it spends a large share of its context before work starts, and keeping one file that long current invites drift. | Medium | Medium | MxM=Medium | Keep reference material (Testing history, Gotchas) in linked files and the file to current state. | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-009 | Selector matching depends on parcel_selectors, pinned to lightningcss's version: its matcher panics on four parsed forms (kept out by the allowlist), and its checked `i32` An+B answers no for `:nth-child(n-2147483647)`. A lightningcss upgrade can add parts the allowlist doesn't know. | Medium | Low | MxL=Low | Bump both together; `the_engine_allowlist` and the selector-engine testbench scenario on every upgrade; report the An+B overflow upstream. | Owner | Mitigating | Low |
| R-010 | Sibling combinators away from the subject stay unsupported: matching works, but a hover flip must restyle elements inside the following sibling, which ADR 0029's scoping doesn't cover. | Low | Medium | LxM=Low | A design change of its own (restyle invalidation across a sibling's subtree) when a page needs it. | Owner | Accepted | Low |

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @CHANGELOG.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0028-modern-authoring-gaps-roadmap.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0034-match-selectors-with-parcel-selectors.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/bug_0028.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/UPSTREAM.md
- @docs/agents/bugs/bug_0179.md
- @docs/agents/skills/testing.md
